card.title: How To Fix an iPhone 7 With No Touch

source.title: How To Fix an iPhone 7 With No Touch

claims.statement: iPhone 7 no-touch is usually pry damage near LCD connector J4502 to a filter/resistor such as FL3917, FL3910 or R3923; trace an OL or short along the touch line to find it.
If all readings are normal, the connector's four ground pins may be pushed in (from repeated screen swaps or fitting an 8/8 Plus screen); bend them out or replace the connector.

procedure: Diode-check J4502 for OL or shorted touch lines.
Inspect FL3917, FL3910, R3923; trace along the line.
If readings normal, bend out the LCD/home button connector ground pins.
Replace the LCD connector if still no touch.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
